description: Feature B — per-batch Edge retry in GCRS so one '/grbi' 'Failed to fetch' no longer blanks the whole GCRS lane (and, transitively, polygon + ads). When GCRS is on the Edge transport and a single batch throws TransportError containing 'Failed to fetch' (or a degraded/empty window), retry THAT batch up to EDGE_BATCH_RETRY_ATTEMPTS with 2s/4s/6s backoff before failure propagates. If retries still fail, DEGRADE: leave that batch's TIDs unresolved so they land in fetch()'s 'errored' list, and CONTINUE the remaining batches. This is safe because tid_polygon_checker already row-aligns an 'Error — SIW unresolved after degraded/poison guards' status for every errored TID (preserving the polygon row-count contract), run_daily.lane_gcrs records errored as counts without raising, and lane_ads already handles a smaller resolved set via ads_missing. mcscli-path behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged. This feature is INDEPENDENT of FEAT-002 (different files, no ordering dependency).
steps: In tools/gcrs_mcscli.py, immediately after BATCH_EDGE add two named constants with a comment referencing the 2026-10-04 Failed-to-fetch run and #G8: EDGE_BATCH_RETRY_ATTEMPTS = 3 and EDGE_BATCH_RETRY_BACKOFF_S = (2, 4, 6). Do NOT change BATCH_EDGE (200) or BATCH_MCSCLI (500).

Add a module-level helper, e.g. _resolve_batch_with_edge_retry(chunk, polygon_set, log, session), that: reads transport = getattr(session,'transport_name',None); if transport != 'edge' it calls _resolve(chunk, polygon_set, log, session) exactly once and returns its result (NO retry, NO catch — preserves mcscli path); if transport == 'edge' it loops up to EDGE_BATCH_RETRY_ATTEMPTS calling _resolve, catching siw_client.TransportError whose message contains 'Failed to fetch' (case-insensitive) OR a degraded/empty window, sleeping EDGE_BATCH_RETRY_BACKOFF_S[attempt] between attempts (guard index), logging a WARNING per retry; on the FINAL failed attempt it logs a WARNING like 'GCRS batch degraded to unresolved after N Edge retries (Failed to fetch); continuing remaining batches' and RETURNS an empty resolution ((empty rows dict, empty invalid set)) so the chunk's TIDs stay unresolved and fall into fetch()'s 'errored' computation. A TransportError that is NOT a Failed-to-fetch/degraded-window error should re-raise unchanged (do not swallow unrelated errors).

In fetch()'s per-batch while loop in tools/gcrs_mcscli.py, replace the direct `chunk_rows, chunk_invalid = _resolve(chunk, polygon_set, log, active_session)` call with `chunk_rows, chunk_invalid = _resolve_batch_with_edge_retry(chunk, polygon_set, log, active_session)`. Leave everything else (batch sizing via _batch_size_for, sequential ordering, offset advance, logging of 'GCRS batch N') unchanged.

Add offline tests in tests/test_polygon_workflow.py following the FailurePathTests fake-session style, patching gcrs_mcscli.time.sleep to no-op: (a) Edge-transport fake session whose first attempt on a batch raises TransportError('Edge SIW grbi request failed: ... Failed to fetch') and the retry succeeds -> assert rows resolve and errored == []; (b) Edge session that raises Failed-to-fetch on EVERY attempt for the first batch but resolves the second batch -> assert fetch() does NOT raise, the first batch's TIDs are in errored, the second batch resolves; (c) mcscli-transport fake session (transport_name='mcscli') that raises a TransportError -> assert it propagates (NOT retried), proving the mcscli path is unchanged. Fake sessions must expose transport_name and ensure_ready so _batch_size_for picks the right size.
acceptance_criteria: tools/gcrs_mcscli.py defines EDGE_BATCH_RETRY_ATTEMPTS=3 and EDGE_BATCH_RETRY_BACKOFF_S=(2,4,6) right after BATCH_EDGE, with a comment citing the 2026-10-04 run and #G8.

An Edge-transport /grbi batch that throws 'Failed to fetch' is retried up to 3 attempts; if all fail, its TIDs appear in fetch()'s returned 'errored' list and the remaining batches still run (fetch does not raise).
An mcscli-transport TransportError is NOT retried and still propagates (mcscli path unchanged).
BATCH_EDGE and BATCH_MCSCLI values are unchanged; /grbi remains strictly sequential.
Running `py -3.13 -m pytest tests/test_polygon_workflow.py -q` passes including the new Feature B tests.
verification: py -3.13 -m pytest tests/test_polygon_workflow.py -q  (all pass, new tests included)
py -3.13 -m pytest tests -q  (full suite still >= 64 passed)
findings: Implemented in tools/gcrs_mcscli.py. Added `from siw_client import ... TransportError` to the existing import. Added EDGE_BATCH_RETRY_ATTEMPTS=3 and EDGE_BATCH_RETRY_BACKOFF_S=(2,4,6) right after BATCH_EDGE with a comment citing the 2026-10-04 run and #G8. Added helper `_is_failed_to_fetch(error)` (case-insensitive match on 'failed to fetch' OR 'degraded') and `_resolve_batch_with_edge_retry(chunk, polygon_set, log, session)`: on non-edge transport it calls `_resolve` exactly once (no retry/catch, mcscli path byte-for-byte unchanged); on edge transport it loops up to EDGE_BATCH_RETRY_ATTEMPTS, catching only Failed-to-fetch/degraded TransportError, sleeping EDGE_BATCH_RETRY_BACKOFF_S[min(attempt,len-1)] between attempts, logging a WARNING per retry, and on the final failed attempt logs 'GCRS batch degraded to unresolved after 3 Edge retries (Failed to fetch); continuing remaining batches' and returns ({}, set()) so the chunk's TIDs land in fetch()'s errored list. Non-Failed-to-fetch TransportErrors re-raise unchanged. fetch()'s per-batch call now uses `_resolve_batch_with_edge_retry`; batch sizing (_batch_size_for), sequential /grbi ordering, offset advance, and 'GCRS batch N' logging are unchanged. BATCH_EDGE(200)/BATCH_MCSCLI(500) unchanged. Added 3 offline tests in tests/test_polygon_workflow.py FailurePathTests (patching gcrs_mcscli.time.sleep): edge retry-then-resolve (errored==[]), edge degrade of first batch with second batch resolving (first batch's TIDs in errored, fetch does not raise), and mcscli TransportError propagates un-retried (1 call). Verification: `py -3.13 -m pytest tests/test_polygon_workflow.py -q` -> 21 passed; `py -3.13 -m pytest tests -q` -> 67 passed (baseline 64). Note for FEAT-002: TransportError is now imported into gcrs_mcscli; no behavioral change to run_daily/run_controller was made here.
